# cfire Language Reference Sheet for LLMs & AI Agents

## Grammar & Syntax Rules
- Package: `package <name>` (canonical entry: `package main`)
  - Same-Directory Package Merging: All `.cf` files in the same directory declaring the same `package <name>` automatically share types, functions, methods, and constants without writing `import "./sibling.cf"` (test-only `*_test.cf` files are excluded from production builds).
  - OS-Conditional Platform Files: Files ending in `*_darwin.cf` / `*_macos.cf`, `*_linux.cf`, `*_windows.cf`, `*_ios.cf`, `*_wasm.cf`, or `*_unix.cf` are compiled only when targeting the matching platform.
- Imports:
  - Foundational Core: `import "core:<module>"` (e.g. `import "core:fs"`, `import "core:json"`, `import "core:net/http"`, `import "core:keychain"`)
  - Domain Extensions: `import "ext:<module>"` (e.g. `import "ext:ai"`, `import "ext:audio"`, `import "ext:compress/zstd"`, `import "ext:crypto/sodium"`, `import "ext:db/sqlite"`, `import "ext:net/ssh"`, `import "ext:tako"`, `import "ext:webui"`)
  - Note on Builtin Operations: Methods and associated items on `str`, numeric types, slices (`[]T`), arrays (`[N]T`), and maps (`map[K]V`) live directly on values/types (`s.trim()`, `s.split(",")`, `xs.sort()`, `m.keys()`, `i32.parse(s)`, `i32.MAX`). Legacy `import "core:str"` and `import "core:sort"` are retired (`cfire/RETIRED-API`).
  - Local package: `import "./path/to/pkg"`
  - Foreign C/C++: `import cpp "header.h"` or `import cpp "header.h" as alias` (preprocessor defines and native linkage — `Defines`, `PkgConfig`, `Libraries`, `Frameworks`, `Includes`, `UrlSchemes`, and `SignIdentity` — belong declaratively in `build.cf` via `build.Executable`/`build.Package`/`build.Define`, or via CLI `--define <K[=V]>` / `-D<K[=V]>` and `--pkg-config <name>`. Legacy `@pkg` and `@define` import attributes are retired via `cfire/RETIRED-API`).
- Variable Declarations & Naming Conventions:
  - Immutable binding (including top-level constants): `x := 42`, `name: str = "cfire"` (no `const` keyword)
  - Mutable binding: `mut y := 10`, `mut count: i64 = 0`
  - Struct fields use `snake_case` (`cfire/FIELD-NAME-CASE`), enum variants use `UpperCamelCase` accessed as `Enum::Variant` or cross-package `pkg.Enum::Variant` (`::` is only for enum variants; use `.` for modules, bounds `pkg.Bound`, methods, and associated items).
  - Integer literals accept decimal, `0x`/`0X` hex, `0b`/`0B` binary, and `0o`/`0O` octal (`0o600`, `0o755`). String literals decode `\xHH`, `\u{HEX}`, and preserve embedded `\x00` bytes without NUL truncation.
- Built-in Prelude Functions & Type Constructors:
  - Standard Output & Error: `println(fmt, ...)` / `print(fmt, ...)` (`stdout`), `eprintln(fmt, ...)` / `eprint(fmt, ...)` (`stderr`)
  - Interactive Terminal Input: `cli.prompt(message: str = "") -> str?` and `cli.prompt_password(message: str = "") -> str?` (`core:cli`); or stream directly from `os.stdin().read_line() -> str?` (`core:os`)
  - Assertions: `assert(cond)`, `assert_eq(a, b)`, `assert_ne(a, b)`, `panic(msg)`
  - Canonical Construction (`make(...)` & Type Constructors `T(x)`, no `as` keyword):
    - Scalar conversions: `i8(x)`, `i16(x)`, `i32(x)`, `i64(x)`, `isize(x)`, `u8(x)`, `byte(x)`, `u16(x)`, `u32(x)`, `u64(x)`, `usize(x)`, `f32(x)`, `f64(x)`, `bool(x)`
    - Byte/u8 slice & string conversions: `[]byte(s_or_slice)`, `[]u8(s_or_slice)`, `str(bytes_or_scalar)`
    - Value/Heap/Collection constructors: `make(T, args...)`, `make(own[T], v)`, `make(shared[T], v)`, `make([]T, len[, cap])`, `make(map[K]V)`
- Strings & Arbitrary Expression Interpolation:
  - Double-quoted strings interpolate arbitrary expressions and optional format specifiers: `"sum={a + b} first={items[0]} hex={mask:04x}"` (lowers to `std::format("sum={} first={} hex={:04x}", a + b, items[0], mask)`)
  - Raw multi-line strings: `` `SELECT * FROM users` ``
- Function Signatures:
  - `fn name(a: i32, mut b: str, move c: []byte) -> Ret! { ... }`
  - Method with receiver: `fn (mut self: Server) start() -> void! { ... }`
  - Fallible return: `-> T!` lowers to `std::expected<T, cfire::Error>`
  - Optional return: `-> T?` lowers to `std::optional<T>`
  - Multi-return tuples: `fn coords() -> (f64, f64) { return (1.0, 2.0) }`, destructuring: `(x, y) := coords()`
  - Generic parameters: `fn process[T: Reader + io.Closer](item: T) { ... }` (compound bounds with `+`, package-qualified bounds `pkg.Bound`, and generic receiver methods `fn (b: Box[T]) get() -> T`)
- Parameter Intent Rules:
  - Default: immutable read-only view (including zero-copy `str` views with implicit copies when stored or returned)
  - `mut`: must pass mutable variable with `mut` at call site: `update(mut val)`
  - `move`: transfers ownership with `move` at call site: `consume(move item)`
- Types:
  - Primitives: `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `isize`, `u8`, `byte`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `usize`, `f32`, `f64`, `bool`, `char`, `void`
  - Strings & Byte Slices: `str`, `[]byte`, `[]u8`
  - Slices & Arrays: `[]T`, `[N]T`
  - Maps: `map[Key]Val`
  - Smart Pointers: `own[T]` (move-only unique ownership), `shared[T]` (reference-counted shared ownership)
  - Foreign Interop Raw Pointers (restricted to `import cpp` FFI boundaries; rejected in pure `.cf` via `cfire/RAW-POINTER`): `*T`, `*mut T`
  - Struct: `type User struct { id: i64, name: str `json:"name"` }`
  - Enum: `type Shape enum { Circle(f64), Rect(f64, f64), None }`
  - Interface: `type Writer interface { fn mut write(b: []byte) -> usize!; fn flush() }` (`fn mut` / `fn (mut self)` for mutable receivers and `mut`/`move` parameter intents)
- Control Flow & RAII Defer:
  - `if cond { ... } else { ... }`
  - Exclusive numeric range loop: `for i in 0..n { ... }` (iterates `0` to `n - 1`)
  - Inclusive numeric range loop: `for i in 1..=n { ... }` (iterates `1` to `n`)
  - Collection loop: `for item in slice { ... }` / `for i, item in slice { ... }`
  - Conditional / unbounded loop: `for cond { ... }` / `for { ... }`
  - Exhaustive pattern match: `match val { pkg.Mode::Read(n) if n > 0 => ..., Shape::Circle(r) => 3.14 * r * r, Shape::Rect(w, h) => w * h }` (pattern bindings are in scope inside `if` guards; guarded arms do not satisfy exhaustiveness on their own)
  - Single-statement or multi-statement RAII scope cleanup: `defer resource.close()` or `defer { f.flush(); f.close() }` (`return` inside `defer { ... }` is rejected via `cfire/RETURN-IN-DEFER`)
- Testing, Fuzzing & Benchmarks:
  - Unit test blocks: `test "description" { ... }`
  - Property-based fuzz blocks: `fuzz "description" |x: i64, s: str| { ... }` (or parameterized `test "name" |x: i64| { ... }`): runs dictionary seeds + deterministic PRNG iterations (`--fuzz-runs <N>`, `--seed <S>`) with automatic counterexample shrinking.
  - Statistical benchmarks: `bench "description" { black_box(work()) }` and parameterized `bench "name" |size in [64, 1024, 16384]| { ... }` or `|k in 1..=4|`.
  - Executable doc-tests & checks: fenced ` ```cf ` blocks inside `///` doc-comments with `assert(...)` / `assert_eq(...)`, open FD leak canary, and `[auto] json round-trip: <StructName>` tests.
- Error (`T!`) & Optional (`T?`) Handling:
  - `val := try fallible()` (early return error on failure)
  - `val := fallible() or fallback_expr`
  - `val := fallible() or err { return -1 }` or parameterless `val := fallible() or { return -1 }` (block must diverge or panic)
  - `val := optional() or fallback_expr`
  - `val := optional() or { return -1 }` (`or err { ... }` on `T?` is rejected via `cfire/OPTIONAL-OR-ERR`)
  - Flow-sensitive narrowing: after `if opt != none { ... }` or `if opt == none { return }`, `opt` narrows to `T`.
- Memory Safety, Loan Tracking & Type Rules:
  - Move Discipline (`cfire/USE-AFTER-MOVE`, `cfire/MOVE-REQUIRED`, `cfire/MOVE-CALLSITE`): Copying or passing a move-only value (`own[T]` or structs containing `own[T]`) or using a variable after `move` without reassigning on all paths is rejected; `move` parameters require `move` at call sites.
  - View & Loan Tracking (`cfire/USE-AFTER-FREE`, `cfire/DANGLING-RETURN`, `cfire/DANGLING-TEMPORARY`, `cfire/ITERATOR-INVALIDATION`): Mutating, reallocating, or moving a container while a view borrows from it or while iterating over it, or returning a view into a local/temporary, is rejected at compile time.
  - Type & Boundary Checks (`cfire/RECURSIVE-TYPE`, `cfire/UNSATISFIED-CONSTRAINT`, `cfire/RAW-POINTER`, `cfire/REFERENCE-TYPE`, `cfire/RETIRED-API`, `cfire/NULL-DEREF`): Direct or optional self-recursive value structs without `own[T]`/`shared[T]`/`[]T` indirection, non-matching interface constraints, pure-`.cf` raw pointers or `&T` references, and unguarded pointer dereferences are rejected at compile time.
  - Bounds, Arithmetic, Tags & Injection (`cfire/INDEX-OUT-OF-BOUNDS`, `cfire/DIVIDE-BY-ZERO`, `cfire/INVALID-STRUCT-TAG`, `cfire/SQL-INJECTION-RISK`, `cfire/SHELL-INJECTION-RISK`): Constant OOB indexing, div-by-zero, duplicate struct tags, and string-concatenated SQL/shell calls are diagnosed at compile time.
- Foreign C/C++: `cpp { /* verbatim C++23 */ }`, `cpp.some_c_func()`, `import cpp "hdr.h"` (defines in `build.cf` `Defines` or CLI `-DK=V`)
- CLI Tooling:
  - `cfire init [--template cli|tako|webui] [--name <pkg>]` / `cfire new <dir> [--template cli|tako|webui]`: Scaffold a new `cfire` project (`build.cf`, `main.cf`, `main_test.cf`, `.gitignore`)
  - `cfire run [--web] [--ios] [--pkg-config <name>] [target]`: Run native binary, iOS Simulator (`--ios`), or WebAssembly app (`--web`)
  - `cfire build [--target wasm|ios-sim|ios] [--portable] [--static] [--universal] [--pkg-config <name>] [--web-profile canvas|cli] [--subsystem gui|cli] [-o <out>] [target]`: Compile native binary, macOS/iOS `.app` bundle, or WebAssembly
  - `cfire clean [--cache] [--all] [--dry-run] [--json] [path|build.cf]`: Remove project `.cfire/` & manifest outputs (and marker-guarded OS/XDG user cache with `--cache`)
  - `cfire check [--json] [--fix] [--verify-cpp] [file|dir]`: Workspace-aware type & safety checker with fix-its
  - `cfire test [--sanitize] [--json] [--filter <pat>] [--bench] [--fuzz-runs <N>] [--seed <S>] [--bench-time <ms>] [file|dir]`: Unit, fuzz, doc-test, and benchmark runner
  - `cfire bench [--json] [--filter <pat>] [--bench-time <ms>] [file|dir]`: Statistical benchmark runner
  - `cfire fix [--only <code,...>] [--dry-run] [--json] [file|dir]`: Auto-fixer applying `MachineApplicable` fixes by default (`EditorOnly` assists such as `cfire/PREFER-ENUM` apply with `--only`)
  - `cfire serve [--port <n>] [--no-open] [target|path]`: Built-in static server with WASM MIME & COOP/COEP headers
  - `cfire eject <file.cf> [out_dir]`: Export standalone ISO C++23 + `CMakeLists.txt`
  - `cfire outline [--json] [file|dir]`: AST symbol & test/fuzz/bench outline
  - `cfire inspect <target|cfire/CODE>`: Inspect symbol, header, module, or diagnostic rule (`cfire inspect cfire/USE-AFTER-MOVE`)
  - `cfire install [--user|--prefix <dir>|--portable <dir>]`: Install self-relocating `cfire` binary and `runtime/` headers
  - `cfire upgrade [--check] [--version <tag>] [--yes] [--force]` (`cfire self-update`): Check for or apply SHA-256 verified binary & runtime upgrades in place
  - `cfire ide [target|--all|--status] [--global]`: Configure LSP, MCP, and agent rules for supported editors/agents
  - `cfire mcp [--setup|--print-config]`: Start built-in Model Context Protocol server over stdio
  - `cfire doc [--check|--llm]`: Synchronize docs/`LLMS.txt` or print this reference sheet
  - `cfire eval 'expr'`: Immediate evaluation of expressions (`DevDebug`)

## Builtin Types & Standard Library (`core:*`, `ext:*`)

### Builtin Types: Methods, Associated Items & make (no import required)
Operations on values of builtin types are methods on the value: `s.trim()`, `xs.sort()`, `m.keys()`, `x.abs()`, `f.sqrt()`. Searches return `T?`, never `-1`. Limits and parsing belong to the type: `i32.MAX`, `f64.NAN`, `i32.parse(s) -> i32!`. Bridge wrappers explicitly via `opt.or_error(msg[, code]) -> T!` and `res.ignore_error() -> T?`. `make` is the one construction builtin, and the type decides where memory lives: `make(T, args)` is a value, `make(own[T], args)` / `make(shared[T], args)` are heap-owned, and `make([]T, len[, cap])` is a slice. In the table, `Self` is the receiver type, `T` the element type and `K`/`V` the map key/value types.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn (x: i64) abs() -> Self`: Absolute value. Integer `MIN.abs()` panics; use `checked_abs` or `wrapping_abs`.
- `fn (x: i64) min(other: Self) -> Self`: Smaller of the two values (for floats, a NaN operand yields the other operand).
- `fn (x: i64) max(other: Self) -> Self`: Larger of the two values (for floats, a NaN operand yields the other operand).
- `fn (x: i64) clamp(lo: Self, hi: Self) -> Self`: Restricts the value to `lo..=hi`; panics when `lo > hi` (or either bound is NaN).
- `fn (x: i64) signum() -> Self`: `-1`, `0` or `1` (floats: `-1.0`, `±0.0`, `1.0`, NaN for NaN).
- `fn (x: i64) pow(exp: Self) -> Self`: Integer power (a negative exponent or overflow panics) or float power.
- `fn (x: i64) count_ones() -> u32`: Number of set bits.
- `fn (x: i64) leading_zeros() -> u32`: Number of leading zero bits.
- `fn (x: i64) trailing_zeros() -> u32`: Number of trailing zero bits.
- `fn (x: i64) is_power_of_two() -> bool`: `true` for 1, 2, 4, …; `false` for zero and negatives.
- `fn (x: i64) div_euclid(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Euclidean division (the remainder is never negative); panics on division by zero or overflow.
- `fn (x: i64) rem_euclid(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Euclidean remainder, always `>= 0`; integer division by zero panics.
- `fn (x: i64) checked_add(rhs: Self) -> Self?`: `none` on overflow.
- `fn (x: i64) checked_sub(rhs: Self) -> Self?`: `none` on overflow.
- `fn (x: i64) checked_mul(rhs: Self) -> Self?`: `none` on overflow.
- `fn (x: i64) checked_div(rhs: Self) -> Self?`: `none` on division by zero or overflow (`MIN / -1`).
- `fn (x: i64) checked_neg() -> Self?`: `none` on overflow (`MIN`, or any non-zero unsigned value).
- `fn (x: i64) checked_abs() -> Self?`: `none` for `MIN`.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_add(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Two's-complement wrapping addition.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_sub(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Two's-complement wrapping subtraction.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_mul(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Two's-complement wrapping multiplication.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_div(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Wrapping division (`MIN / -1 == MIN`); division by zero panics.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_neg() -> Self`: Two's-complement wrapping negation.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_abs() -> Self`: Absolute value, wrapping for `MIN`.
- `fn (x: i64) saturating_add(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Addition clamped to `MIN..=MAX`.
- `fn (x: i64) saturating_sub(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Subtraction clamped to `MIN..=MAX`.
- `fn (x: i64) saturating_mul(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Multiplication clamped to `MIN..=MAX`.
- `fn (x: i64) saturating_div(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Division clamped to `MIN..=MAX` (`MIN / -1 == MAX`); division by zero panics.
- `fn (x: i64) saturating_neg() -> Self`: Negation clamped to `MIN..=MAX`.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_shl(bits: u32) -> Self`: Left shift with the count taken modulo the bit width.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_shr(bits: u32) -> Self`: Right shift with the count taken modulo the bit width.
- `fn (x: i64) checked_shl(bits: u32) -> Self?`: `none` when the count is `>=` the bit width.
- `fn (x: i64) checked_shr(bits: u32) -> Self?`: `none` when the count is `>=` the bit width.
- `fn (x: i64) wrapping_as()`: Conversion to `T` that wraps on overflow: `x.wrapping_as[u8]()`.
- `fn (x: i64) saturating_as()`: Conversion to `T` that clamps on overflow: `x.saturating_as[u8]()`.
- `fn (x: i64) try_as()`: Conversion to `T?`, `none` when the value does not fit: `x.try_as[u8]()`.
- `fn (f: f64) abs() -> Self`: Absolute value. Integer `MIN.abs()` panics; use `checked_abs` or `wrapping_abs`.
- `fn (f: f64) min(other: Self) -> Self`: Smaller of the two values (for floats, a NaN operand yields the other operand).
- `fn (f: f64) max(other: Self) -> Self`: Larger of the two values (for floats, a NaN operand yields the other operand).
- `fn (f: f64) clamp(lo: Self, hi: Self) -> Self`: Restricts the value to `lo..=hi`; panics when `lo > hi` (or either bound is NaN).
- `fn (f: f64) signum() -> Self`: `-1`, `0` or `1` (floats: `-1.0`, `±0.0`, `1.0`, NaN for NaN).
- `fn (f: f64) pow(exp: Self) -> Self`: Integer power (a negative exponent or overflow panics) or float power.
- `fn (f: f64) rem_euclid(rhs: Self) -> Self`: Euclidean remainder, always `>= 0`; integer division by zero panics.
- `fn (f: f64) wrapping_as()`: Conversion to `T` that wraps on overflow: `x.wrapping_as[u8]()`.
- `fn (f: f64) saturating_as()`: Conversion to `T` that clamps on overflow: `x.saturating_as[u8]()`.
- `fn (f: f64) try_as()`: Conversion to `T?`, `none` when the value does not fit: `x.try_as[u8]()`.
- `fn (f: f64) floor() -> Self`: Largest integer value `<=` x.
- `fn (f: f64) ceil() -> Self`: Smallest integer value `>=` x.
- `fn (f: f64) round() -> Self`: Nearest integer value, halfway cases away from zero.
- `fn (f: f64) trunc() -> Self`: Integer part, rounding toward zero.
- `fn (f: f64) fract() -> Self`: Fractional part, `x - x.trunc()`.
- `fn (f: f64) sqrt() -> Self`: Square root (NaN for negative input).
- `fn (f: f64) cbrt() -> Self`: Cube root.
- `fn (f: f64) powi(exp: i32) -> Self`: Raises to an integer power.
- `fn (f: f64) exp() -> Self`: `e` raised to x.
- `fn (f: f64) ln() -> Self`: Natural logarithm.
- `fn (f: f64) log2() -> Self`: Base-2 logarithm.
- `fn (f: f64) log10() -> Self`: Base-10 logarithm.
- `fn (f: f64) sin() -> Self`: Sine (radians).
- `fn (f: f64) cos() -> Self`: Cosine (radians).
- `fn (f: f64) tan() -> Self`: Tangent (radians).
- `fn (f: f64) asin() -> Self`: Arcsine, in radians.
- `fn (f: f64) acos() -> Self`: Arccosine, in radians.
- `fn (f: f64) atan() -> Self`: Arctangent, in radians (see `math.atan2` for two inputs).
- `fn (f: f64) sinh() -> Self`: Hyperbolic sine.
- `fn (f: f64) cosh() -> Self`: Hyperbolic cosine.
- `fn (f: f64) tanh() -> Self`: Hyperbolic tangent.
- `fn (f: f64) to_degrees() -> Self`: Converts radians to degrees.
- `fn (f: f64) to_radians() -> Self`: Converts degrees to radians.
- `fn (f: f64) is_nan() -> bool`: `true` for NaN.
- `fn (f: f64) is_inf() -> bool`: `true` for `+inf` or `-inf`.
- `fn (f: f64) is_finite() -> bool`: `true` unless NaN or infinite.
- `fn (s: str) len() -> usize`: Number of elements (bytes for `str`).
- `fn (s: str) is_empty() -> bool`: `true` when `len() == 0`.
- `fn (s: str) contains(sub: str) -> bool`: `true` if the substring occurs.
- `fn (s: str) starts_with(prefix: str) -> bool`: `true` if `s` begins with `prefix`.
- `fn (s: str) ends_with(suffix: str) -> bool`: `true` if `s` ends with `suffix`.
- `fn (s: str) index_of(needle: str, start: usize = default) -> usize?`: Byte position of the first occurrence at or after `start` (default 0), or `none`.
- `fn (s: str) last_index_of(needle: str) -> usize?`: Byte position of the last occurrence, or `none`.
- `fn (s: str) split(sep: str) -> []str`: Splits on every occurrence of `sep` (an empty `s` gives one empty part).
- `fn (s: str) split_n(sep: str, n: usize) -> []str`: Splits into at most `n` parts; the last part holds the rest.
- `fn (s: str) lines() -> []str`: Splits on `\n`, dropping a trailing `\r` from each line and a final empty line.
- `fn (s: str) trim() -> str`: View without leading and trailing ASCII whitespace.
- `fn (s: str) trim_start() -> str`: View without leading ASCII whitespace.
- `fn (s: str) trim_end() -> str`: View without trailing ASCII whitespace.
- `fn (s: str) strip_prefix(prefix: str) -> str?`: View after `prefix`, or `none` if `s` does not start with it.
- `fn (s: str) strip_suffix(suffix: str) -> str?`: View before `suffix`, or `none` if `s` does not end with it.
- `fn (s: str) replace(from: str, to: str) -> str`: Copy with the first occurrence of `from` replaced.
- `fn (s: str) replace_all(from: str, to: str) -> str`: Copy with every occurrence of `from` replaced.
- `fn (s: str) repeat(n: usize) -> str`: `s` concatenated `n` times.
- `fn (s: str) to_upper() -> str`: ASCII upper-case copy.
- `fn (s: str) to_lower() -> str`: ASCII lower-case copy.
- `fn (s: str) runes() -> []u32`: Unicode code points (invalid UTF-8 bytes decode as U+FFFD).
- `fn (s: str) rune_count() -> usize`: Number of Unicode code points.
- `fn (s: str) bytes() -> []byte`: The UTF-8 bytes of `s`.
- `fn (s: str) pop() -> T?`: Removes and returns the last element (last byte for `str`), or `none` when empty.
- `fn (s: str) with_ext(ext: str) -> str`: Path with its extension replaced.
- `fn (xs: []T) len() -> usize`: Number of elements (bytes for `str`).
- `fn (xs: []T) is_empty() -> bool`: `true` when `len() == 0`.
- `fn (xs: []T) pop() -> T?`: Removes and returns the last element (last byte for `str`), or `none` when empty.
- `fn (xs: []T) contains(val: T) -> bool`: `true` if an element equals `v`.
- `fn (xs: []T) index_of(val: T) -> usize?`: Position of the first element equal to `v`, or `none`.
- `fn (xs: []T) first() -> T?`: Copy of the first element, or `none` when empty.
- `fn (xs: []T) last() -> T?`: Copy of the last element, or `none` when empty.
- `fn (xs: []T) reverse()`: Reverses the elements in place.
- `fn (xs: []T) sort()`: Sorts in place, ascending.
- `fn (xs: []T) sort_by(cmp: fn(T, T) -> bool)`: Sorts in place with a strict `less(a, b)` comparator.
- `fn (xs: []T) is_sorted() -> bool`: `true` if the elements are in ascending order.
- `fn (xs: []T) binary_search(val: T) -> usize?`: Position of `v` in an ascending sequence, or `none`.
- `fn (xs: []T) join(sep: str) -> str`: Concatenates a `[]str` with `sep` between elements.
- `fn (xs: []T) push(val: T)`: Appends `v`.
- `fn (xs: []T) insert(idx: usize, val: T)`: Inserts `v` at `i`, shifting later elements; panics when `i > len()`.
- `fn (xs: []T) remove(idx: usize) -> T`: Removes and returns the element at `i`, shifting later elements; panics when out of range.
- `fn (xs: []T) swap_remove(idx: usize) -> T`: Removes the element at `i` by moving the last one into its place (O(1)); panics when out of range.
- `fn (xs: []T) truncate(n: usize)`: Keeps the first `n` elements (no effect when `n >= len()`).
- `fn (xs: []T) extend(other: []T)`: Appends a copy of every element of `other`.
- `fn (xs: []T) clear()`: Removes every element.
- `fn (xs: []T) bytes() -> []byte`: Byte view of the slice's storage.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) len() -> usize`: Number of elements (bytes for `str`).
- `fn (arr: [N]T) is_empty() -> bool`: `true` when `len() == 0`.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) contains(val: T) -> bool`: `true` if an element equals `v`.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) index_of(val: T) -> usize?`: Position of the first element equal to `v`, or `none`.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) first() -> T?`: Copy of the first element, or `none` when empty.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) last() -> T?`: Copy of the last element, or `none` when empty.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) reverse()`: Reverses the elements in place.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) sort()`: Sorts in place, ascending.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) sort_by(cmp: fn(T, T) -> bool)`: Sorts in place with a strict `less(a, b)` comparator.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) is_sorted() -> bool`: `true` if the elements are in ascending order.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) binary_search(val: T) -> usize?`: Position of `v` in an ascending sequence, or `none`.
- `fn (arr: [N]T) join(sep: str) -> str`: Concatenates a `[]str` with `sep` between elements.
- `fn (m: map[K]V) len() -> usize`: Number of elements (bytes for `str`).
- `fn (m: map[K]V) is_empty() -> bool`: `true` when `len() == 0`.
- `fn (m: map[K]V) clear()`: Removes every element.
- `fn (m: map[K]V) contains(key: K) -> bool`: `true` if the key is present.
- `fn (m: map[K]V) get(key: K) -> V?`: Copy of the value for `k`, or `none`.
- `fn (m: map[K]V) insert(key: K, val: V) -> V?`: Sets `k` to `v`; returns the previous value, or `none`.
- `fn (m: map[K]V) remove(key: K) -> V?`: Removes `k`; returns its value, or `none` if absent.
- `fn (m: map[K]V) keys() -> []K`: Copy of the keys, in unspecified order.
- `fn (m: map[K]V) values() -> []V`: Copy of the values, in unspecified order.
- `fn (opt: T?) or_error(msg: str, code: i32 = default) -> T!`: Promote `none` into an error value lazily, unwrapping `some`.
- `fn (res: T!) ignore_error() -> T?`: Discard the error of a non-void fallible value, yielding `T?`.
- `const <int>.MAX: Self`: Largest value of the type.
- `const <int>.MIN: Self`: Smallest value of the type.
- `const <int>.BITS: u32`: Width in bits (`u32`).
- `const <float>.MAX: Self`: Largest finite value.
- `const <float>.MIN: Self`: Most negative finite value.
- `const <float>.MIN_POSITIVE: Self`: Smallest positive normal value.
- `const <float>.EPSILON: Self`: Difference between `1.0` and the next representable value.
- `const <float>.INF: Self`: Positive infinity.
- `const <float>.NEG_INF: Self`: Negative infinity.
- `const <float>.NAN: Self`: Not a number.
- `fn T.parse(s: str) -> T!`: Parses a complete literal of any numeric type or `bool` (surrounding whitespace ignored; `bool` accepts `true`/`false`/`1`/`0`), returning an `Error` on empty, invalid, or out-of-range input.
- `make(T) / make(T, args...)`: A value of `T`: default field values, or the type's constructor `fn (T) make(...) -> T` (one per type).
- `make(own[T], args...) / make(shared[T], args...)`: A heap-owned `T` (`unique_ptr` / `shared_ptr`), built from one `T` value or the constructor's arguments.
- `make([]T, len) / make([]T, len, cap)`: `len` zero-filled elements, optionally with `cap` reserved; a negative size or `cap < len` panics.
- `make(map[K]V)`: An empty map (iteration order is unspecified).
- `fn (o: own[T]) release() -> *mut T`: Gives up ownership for C interop: returns the raw pointer and moves `o`, so any later use is `cfire/USE-AFTER-MOVE`. Not available on `shared[T]`.
- `fn own[T].from_raw(p: *mut T) -> own[T]`: Takes ownership of a pointer produced by `release`. Adopting any other pointer is undefined behavior.

### `import "core:build"` (alias: `build`)
Declarative build manifest module (`build.cf`) for configuring packages (`build.Package`), native/GUI/WebAssembly/iOS executables (`build.Executable`, `build.App`), static/shared libraries (`build.Library`), pre-build codegen steps (`build.Step`, `build.Command`), C/C++ source targets (`build.CC`), external CMake/Make/Ninja/Git/Archive dependencies (`build.CMake`, `build.Make`, `build.Ninja`, `build.Git`, `build.Archive`), native pkg-config/library/include/define/framework settings (`build.PkgConfig`, `build.Link`, `build.Libraries`, `build.Include`, `build.Includes`, `build.Define`, `build.Defines`, `build.Frameworks`), and compile-time host/target queries (`build.os()`, `build.arch()`).
Types:
- `Package`: In `build.cf`: declares package metadata and manifest-level `PkgConfig`, `Libraries`, `Frameworks`, `Includes`, and `Defines`.
- `Executable`: In `build.cf`: declares an executable target (`build.Executable(name, { Entry: ... })`).
- `App`: In `build.cf`: alias for `build.Executable(...)`.
- `Library`: In `build.cf`: declares a static or shared library target.
- `Step`: In `build.cf`: a code-generation step run when its inputs are newer than its outputs.
- `CC`: In `build.cf`: compiles C or C++ sources into the project (`build.CC({ Sources: [...] })`).
- `CMake`: In `build.cf`: an external CMake project built as a dependency.
- `Make`: In `build.cf`: an external Make project built as a dependency.
- `Ninja`: In `build.cf`: an external Ninja project built as a dependency.
- `Git`: In `build.cf`: a dependency fetched from a Git repository at a pinned revision.
- `Archive`: In `build.cf`: a dependency fetched as a checksummed archive.
- `Command`: In `build.cf`: a command run as part of the build.
- `PkgConfig`: In `build.cf`: links one or more libraries found through pkg-config.
- `Link`: In `build.cf`: links a library by name.
- `Include`: In `build.cf`: adds a header search directory.
- `Define`: In `build.cf`: adds a C/C++ preprocessor macro definition (`-DKEY` or `-DKEY=VAL`).
- `Defines`: In `build.cf`: adds one or more C/C++ preprocessor macro definitions (`str`, `[]str`, or `{ KEY: VALUE }` map).
- `Libraries`: In `build.cf`: links one or more libraries by name.
- `Includes`: In `build.cf`: adds one or more header search directories.
- `Frameworks`: In `build.cf`: adds one or more Apple frameworks.
- `Target`: In `build.cf`: what `build.Executable` and `build.Library` return.
- `StepTarget`: In `build.cf`: what `build.Step` and `build.Command` return.
- `DepTarget`: In `build.cf`: what `build.CC`, `build.CMake`, `build.Make`, `build.Ninja`, `build.Git`, and `build.Archive` return.
- `PackageTarget`: In `build.cf`: what `build.Package` returns.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn Package(cfg: any, extra: any = {}) -> PackageTarget` (call: `build.Package`): Declares package metadata and manifest-level native defaults (`Name`, `PkgConfig`, `Libraries`, `Frameworks`, `Includes`, `Defines`, `Entry`, `OutDir`).
- `fn Executable(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> Target` (call: `build.Executable`): Declares an executable build target with `Entry`, `Subsystem` (`"cli"` or `"gui"`), `OutDir`, `Targets` (`["native", "wasm", "ios-sim"]`), `WebProfile`, `BundleId`, `AppName`, `Icon` (`.png`/`.svg`/`.icns`/`.ico`), `Sources`, `Includes`, `Defines`, `Flags`, `PkgConfig`, `Libraries`, `Frameworks`, `Portable`, `Static`, `Universal`, `UrlSchemes`, and `SignIdentity`.
- `fn App(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> Target` (call: `build.App`): Alias for `build.Executable` declaring an application executable target.
- `fn Library(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> Target` (call: `build.Library`): Declares a static or shared C/C++/cfire library target with `Sources`, `Includes`, `Defines`, `Flags`, `PkgConfig`, `Libraries`, and `Frameworks`.
- `fn Step(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> StepTarget` (call: `build.Step`): Declares a custom build step executing `Command` and `Args` in `WorkDir` whenever `Inputs` are newer than `Outputs`.
- `fn CC(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> DepTarget` (call: `build.CC`): Compiles C or C++ `Sources` with `Includes`, `Defines`, and `Flags` directly into the native build.
- `fn CMake(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> DepTarget` (call: `build.CMake`): Declares an external CMake dependency (`Url`, `Commit`/`Branch`/`Tag`, `Sha256`, `Includes`, `Defines`, `Flags`, `Target`, `Static`, `Driver`).
- `fn Make(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> DepTarget` (call: `build.Make`): Declares an external GNU Make dependency (`Url`, `Branch`/`Tag`/`Commit`, `Target`, `Includes`, `Flags`).
- `fn Ninja(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> DepTarget` (call: `build.Ninja`): Declares an external Ninja dependency (`Url`, `Branch`/`Tag`/`Commit`, `Target`, `Includes`, `Flags`).
- `fn Git(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> DepTarget` (call: `build.Git`): Fetches a pinned Git dependency (`Url`, `Commit`/`Branch`/`Tag`, `Driver`, `Target`, `Includes`, `Flags`).
- `fn Archive(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> DepTarget` (call: `build.Archive`): Fetches and verifies a source archive dependency (`Url`, `Sha256`, `Driver`, `Includes`, `Flags`).
- `fn Command(name_or_cfg: any, cfg: any = {}) -> StepTarget` (call: `build.Command`): Alias for `build.Step` declaring a custom pre-build command step.
- `fn Link(lib: str)` (call: `build.Link`): Adds a system library (`"sqlite3"`) or Apple framework (`"-framework Security"`) to the linker flags.
- `fn Include(dir: str)` (call: `build.Include`): Adds a relative or absolute header search directory (`-I<dir>`) for `import cpp` headers.
- `fn Define(key: str, value: any = "")` (call: `build.Define`): Adds a C/C++ preprocessor macro definition (`-DKEY` or `-DKEY=VAL`) for `import cpp` headers and native C/C++ sources.
- `fn Defines(defs: any)` (call: `build.Defines`): Adds one or more C/C++ preprocessor macro definitions (`str`, `[]str`, or `{ KEY: VALUE }` map) for `import cpp` headers and native targets.
- `fn PkgConfig(pkg: any)` (call: `build.PkgConfig`): Queries `pkg-config --cflags --libs` for a package name or list of package names (`str` or `[]str`) and links the resolved flags into the build.
- `fn Libraries(libs: any)` (call: `build.Libraries`): Adds one or more native libraries (`str` or `[]str`) to the linker flags.
- `fn Includes(dirs: any)` (call: `build.Includes`): Adds one or more header search directories (`str` or `[]str`) for `import cpp` headers.
- `fn Frameworks(frameworks: any)` (call: `build.Frameworks`): Adds one or more Apple frameworks (`str` or `[]str`) on macOS/iOS builds.
- `fn os() -> str` (call: `build.os`): Returns the target operating system identifier (`"macos"`, `"linux"`, `"windows"`, `"ios"`, `"wasm"`).
- `fn arch() -> str` (call: `build.arch`): Returns the target CPU architecture identifier (`"arm64"`, `"x86_64"`, `"wasm32"`).

### `import "core:cli"` (alias: `cli`)
Generates zero-boilerplate command-line flag parsers from struct field tags (`cli:"--flag,help"`), subcommand/positional argument helpers, and interactive terminal prompts.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn parse[T](args: []str = []) -> T!` (call: `cli.parse`): Parses and validates CLI flags (`str`, `i64`, `i32`, `u16`, `f64`, `bool`) into a tagged struct `T`, returning an `Error` if any numeric or boolean flag argument is invalid.
- `fn args() -> []str` (call: `cli.args`): Returns the raw command-line arguments passed to the process (excluding `argv[0]`).
- `fn subcommand() -> str` (call: `cli.subcommand`): Returns the first non-flag positional argument (subcommand name) or `""` if none.
- `fn positional() -> []str` (call: `cli.positional`): Returns all non-flag positional arguments passed on the command line.
- `fn prompt(message: str = "") -> str?` (call: `cli.prompt`): Prints `message` to stderr and reads a line from stdin without trailing newline, or `none` on EOF.
- `fn prompt_password(message: str = "") -> str?` (call: `cli.prompt_password`): Prints `message` to stderr with terminal echo disabled (`termios` `~ECHO`) and reads a password line from stdin, or `none` on EOF.

### `import "core:collections"` (alias: `collections`)
Standard generic containers backed by STL unordered_set, priority_queue, and deque.
Types:
- `Set[T]`: An unordered set of unique values.
- `Deque[T]`: A double-ended queue: push and pop at both ends in constant time.
- `PriorityQueue[T]`: A max-heap: `pop()` returns the largest value first, or `none` when empty.
- `MinQueue[T]`: A min-heap: `pop()` returns the smallest value first, or `none` when empty.
Functions & Methods:
- `type Set[T] struct` (call: `collections.Set`): Generic hash set container.
- `fn (mut s: Set[T]) insert(val: T) -> bool`: Inserts `val` into the set; returns `true` if `val` was newly inserted.
- `fn (s: Set[T]) contains(val: T) -> bool`: Returns `true` if `val` is present in the set.
- `fn (mut s: Set[T]) remove(val: T) -> bool`: Removes `val` from the set; returns `true` if it was present.
- `fn (s: Set[T]) len() -> usize`: Returns the number of elements in the set.
- `fn (s: Set[T]) empty() -> bool`: Returns `true` when the set has no elements.
- `fn (mut s: Set[T]) clear()`: Removes every element from the set.
- `fn (s: Set[T]) to_slice() -> []T`: Returns a newly allocated slice containing a copy of every element in unspecified order.
- `type PriorityQueue[T] struct` (call: `collections.PriorityQueue`): Max-first priority queue: `push(v)`, `pop() -> T?`, `peek() -> T?`, `len()`, `empty()`.
- `fn (mut pq: PriorityQueue[T]) push(val: T)`: Pushes `val` into the max-first priority queue.
- `fn (pq: PriorityQueue[T]) peek() -> T?`: Returns a copy of the largest element without removing it, or `none` when empty.
- `fn (pq: PriorityQueue[T]) top() -> T`: Returns the largest element (panics when empty).
- `fn (mut pq: PriorityQueue[T]) pop() -> T?`: Removes and returns the largest element, or `none` when empty.
- `fn (pq: PriorityQueue[T]) len() -> usize`: Returns the number of queued elements.
- `fn (pq: PriorityQueue[T]) empty() -> bool`: Returns `true` when the priority queue is empty.
- `type MinQueue[T] struct` (call: `collections.MinQueue`): Min-first priority queue (smallest element pops first), with the same methods as `PriorityQueue[T]`. Tuples order element by element, so `MinQueue[(i64, i64)]` pops the lowest cost first.
- `fn (mut q: MinQueue[T]) push(val: T)`: Pushes `val` into the min-first priority queue.
- `fn (q: MinQueue[T]) peek() -> T?`: Returns a copy of the smallest element without removing it, or `none` when empty.
- `fn (q: MinQueue[T]) top() -> T`: Returns the smallest element (panics when empty).
- `fn (mut q: MinQueue[T]) pop() -> T?`: Removes and returns the smallest element, or `none` when empty.
- `fn (q: MinQueue[T]) len() -> usize`: Returns the number of queued elements.
- `fn (q: MinQueue[T]) empty() -> bool`: Returns `true` when the min-queue is empty.
- `type Deque[T] struct` (call: `collections.Deque`): Generic double-ended queue.
- `fn (mut d: Deque[T]) push_back(val: T)`: Appends `val` to the back of the deque.
- `fn (mut d: Deque[T]) push_front(val: T)`: Prepends `val` to the front of the deque.
- `fn (mut d: Deque[T]) pop_back() -> T`: Removes and returns the back element.
- `fn (mut d: Deque[T]) pop_front() -> T`: Removes and returns the front element.
- `fn (d: Deque[T]) at(idx: usize) -> T?`: Returns the element at `idx`, or `none` when `idx >= len()`.
- `fn (d: Deque[T]) len() -> usize`: Returns the number of elements in the deque.
- `fn (d: Deque[T]) empty() -> bool`: Returns `true` when the deque is empty.
- `fn (mut d: Deque[T]) clear()`: Removes every element from the deque.

### `import "core:crypto/aes"` (alias: `aes`)
Constant-time AES-256 block cipher implementation with Counter Mode (CTR) and Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD).
Types:
- `GcmResult`: The output of AES-256-GCM encryption.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn generate_key() -> []byte` (call: `aes.generate_key`): Generates a 32-byte (256-bit) cryptographically secure AES-256 key from OS entropy.
- `fn encrypt(key: []byte, plaintext: []byte, aad: []byte = []) -> []byte!` (call: `aes.encrypt`): Encrypts `plaintext` with AES-256-GCM using a fresh 12-byte random nonce and returns `[12-byte nonce || ciphertext || 16-byte tag]`.
- `fn decrypt(key: []byte, combined: []byte, aad: []byte = []) -> []byte!` (call: `aes.decrypt`): Authenticates and decrypts a combined `[12-byte nonce || ciphertext || 16-byte tag]` AES-256-GCM payload.
- `fn encrypt_gcm(key: []byte, nonce: []byte, plaintext: []byte, aad: []byte = []) -> GcmResult!` (call: `aes.encrypt_gcm`): Encrypts plaintext with AES-256-GCM AEAD, producing ciphertext and a 16-byte authentication tag.
- `fn decrypt_gcm(key: []byte, nonce: []byte, ciphertext: []byte, tag: []byte, aad: []byte = []) -> []byte!` (call: `aes.decrypt_gcm`): Authenticates and decrypts AES-256-GCM ciphertext, failing if tag verification fails or data was tampered.
- `fn encrypt_ctr(key: []byte, iv: []byte, plaintext: []byte) -> []byte!` (call: `aes.encrypt_ctr`): Encrypts plaintext using AES-256-CTR mode.
- `fn decrypt_ctr(key: []byte, iv: []byte, ciphertext: []byte) -> []byte!` (call: `aes.decrypt_ctr`): Decrypts ciphertext using AES-256-CTR mode.
- `fn decrypt_gcm_str(key: []byte, nonce: []byte, ct: []byte, tag: []byte, aad: []byte = []) -> str!` (call: `aes.decrypt_gcm_str`): Decrypts an authenticated AES-GCM ciphertext and validates the tag, returning a UTF-8 string.

### `import "core:crypto/blake3"` (alias: `blake3`)
Computes fast 256-bit cryptographic hex digests over byte slices (convenience alias for `core:crypto/sha256`).
Functions & Methods:
- `fn hash_hex(data: []byte) -> str` (call: `blake3.hash_hex`): Returns a 64-character lowercase hex digest of `data`.

### `import "core:crypto/hmac"` (alias: `hmac`)
Computes RFC 2104 keyed HMAC-SHA256 authentication digests, RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256 derived keys, and RFC 8018 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password-derived keys.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn sha256_hex(key: str, data: str) -> str` (call: `hmac.sha256_hex`): Returns a 64-character lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 digest.
- `fn sha256_bytes(key: []byte, data: []byte) -> []byte` (call: `hmac.sha256_bytes`): Computes HMAC-SHA256 over raw byte slices.
- `fn verify(key: str, data: str, mac: str) -> bool` (call: `hmac.verify`): Verifies in constant time whether `mac` matches the computed HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of `data` under `key`.
- `fn equal(a: str, b: str) -> bool` (call: `hmac.equal`): Performs a constant-time equality check on two MAC digests to prevent timing attacks.
- `fn hkdf_sha256(ikm: []byte, salt: []byte = [], info: []byte = [], length: usize = 32) -> []byte` (call: `hmac.hkdf_sha256`): Derives cryptographic key material of `length` bytes using RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256 Extract-and-Expand.
- `fn hkdf_sha256_hex(ikm: str, salt: str = "", info: str = "", length: usize = 32) -> str` (call: `hmac.hkdf_sha256_hex`): Derives a hex-encoded key string using RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256.
- `fn pbkdf2_sha256(password: str, salt: []byte, iterations: u32 = 600000, length: usize = 32) -> []byte` (call: `hmac.pbkdf2_sha256`): Derives a cryptographic key of `length` bytes from `password` and `salt` using RFC 8018 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256.

### `import "core:crypto/sha256"` (alias: `sha256`)
Computes NIST FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 digests and generates OS-backed cryptographically secure random bytes (`arc4random_buf` / `/dev/urandom`).
Functions & Methods:
- `fn hash_hex(data: []byte) -> str` (call: `sha256.hash_hex`): Returns a 64-character lowercase hex digest of `data`.
- `fn hash_bytes(data: []byte) -> []byte` (call: `sha256.hash_bytes`): Returns 32-byte binary SHA-256 digest of `data`.
- `fn random_bytes(n: usize) -> []byte` (call: `sha256.random_bytes`): Generates `n` cryptographically secure random bytes from the OS CSPRNG.
- `fn random_hex(n: usize = 32) -> str` (call: `sha256.random_hex`): Generates `n` cryptographically secure random bytes encoded as a `2*n`-character lowercase hex string.
- `fn hash_file_hex(path: str) -> str!` (call: `sha256.hash_file_hex`): Computes the hex-encoded SHA-256 digest of a file on disk.

### `import "core:encoding/base64"` (alias: `base64`)
High-performance, zero-allocation Base64 and URL-safe Base64 encoder and decoder.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn encode(data: []byte, url_safe: bool = false) -> str` (call: `base64.encode`): Encodes binary byte slice into standard or URL-safe Base64 string.
- `fn encode_str(s: str, url_safe: bool = false) -> str` (call: `base64.encode_str`): Encodes a UTF-8 text string into standard or URL-safe Base64.
- `fn decode(s: str) -> []byte!` (call: `base64.decode`): Decodes a Base64 string into binary bytes.
- `fn decode_str(s: str) -> str!` (call: `base64.decode_str`): Decodes a Base64 string into a UTF-8 text string.

### `import "core:encoding/csv"` (alias: `csv`)
RFC 4180 compliant CSV parser and serializer supporting multi-line quoted fields and comma escaping.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn parse(s: str) -> [][]str!` (call: `csv.parse`): Parses an RFC 4180 CSV string into a 2D table of rows and columns, returning an `Error` on malformed or unclosed quotes.
- `fn stringify(rows: [][]str) -> str` (call: `csv.stringify`): Serializes a 2D table of strings into an RFC 4180 formatted CSV string.
- `fn read_all(path: str) -> [][]str!` (call: `csv.read_all`): Reads an entire CSV file from disk and parses it into rows.
- `fn write_all(path: str, rows: [][]str) -> void!` (call: `csv.write_all`): Serializes rows to CSV and writes to disk.

### `import "core:encoding/hex"` (alias: `hex`)
Encodes binary bytes to lowercase hexadecimal strings and decodes hex strings to byte buffers.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn encode(data: []byte) -> str` (call: `hex.encode`): Encodes binary bytes to lowercase hexadecimal string.
- `fn encode_str(s: str) -> str` (call: `hex.encode_str`): Encodes text characters to hexadecimal string.
- `fn decode(s: str) -> []byte!` (call: `hex.decode`): Decodes a hexadecimal string to binary bytes.
- `fn decode_str(s: str) -> str!` (call: `hex.decode_str`): Decodes a hexadecimal string to a UTF-8 string.

### `import "core:fs"` (alias: `fs`)
Provides RAII file and directory utilities backed by `std::filesystem` and `std::vector<std::uint8_t>` with strict `_bytes` / `_text` symmetry.
Types:
- `OpenMode`: How `fs.open` opens a file.
- `SeekWhence`: The origin for `file.seek`.
- `File`: An unbuffered OS file handle, closed automatically when it goes out of scope.
- `FileInfo`: File, directory, or symbolic link metadata returned by `fs.stat`.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn read_bytes(path: str) -> []byte!` (call: `fs.read_bytes`): Reads an entire binary file into a byte buffer.
- `fn write_bytes(path: str, data: []byte) -> void!` (call: `fs.write_bytes`): Writes a byte slice to disk (truncating any existing file).
- `fn append_bytes(path: str, data: []byte) -> void!` (call: `fs.append_bytes`): Appends a byte slice to a file on disk (creating the file if it does not exist).
- `fn read_text(path: str) -> str!` (call: `fs.read_text`): Reads an entire UTF-8 text file into a `str`.
- `fn write_text(path: str, text: str) -> void!` (call: `fs.write_text`): Writes a UTF-8 string to disk.
- `fn append_text(path: str, text: str) -> void!` (call: `fs.append_text`): Appends a UTF-8 string to a file on disk.
- `fn rename(from: str, to: str) -> void!` (call: `fs.rename`): Renames or moves a file or directory.
- `fn copy_file(from: str, to: str) -> void!` (call: `fs.copy_file`): Copies a file from `from` to `to` (overwriting `to` if it exists).
- `fn file_size(path: str) -> u64!` (call: `fs.file_size`): Returns the size of a file in bytes.
- `fn open(path: str, mode: OpenMode = OpenMode::Read) -> File!` (call: `fs.open`): Opens a file with specified mode (Read, Write, Append, ReadWrite) returning an unbuffered OS descriptor `File` handle.
- `fn create_new(path: str, mode: u32 = 0o600) -> File!` (call: `fs.create_new`): Atomically creates a new file with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` (`CREATE_NEW`), failing with `ERR_EXISTS` if it already exists.
- `fn stat(path: str) -> FileInfo!` (call: `fs.stat`): Inspects metadata (`size`, `mtime_ms`, `mode`, `is_dir`, `is_symlink`) for a file, directory, or symlink.
- `fn realpath(path: str) -> str!` (call: `fs.realpath`): Resolves `.` / `..` segments and symbolic links to an existing canonical path.
- `const ERR_EXISTS: i32` (call: `fs.ERR_EXISTS`): `Error.code()` value when a path already exists (`EEXIST`).
- `const ERR_NOT_FOUND: i32` (call: `fs.ERR_NOT_FOUND`): `Error.code()` value when a file or directory does not exist (`ENOENT`).
- `const ERR_PERMISSION: i32` (call: `fs.ERR_PERMISSION`): `Error.code()` value on permission denial (`EACCES` / `EPERM`).
- `fn (f: File) fd() -> i32`: Returns the underlying OS file descriptor (`-1` if closed).
- `fn (f: File) is_open() -> bool`: Returns `true` if the file handle holds a valid open file descriptor.
- `fn (f: File) is_tty() -> bool`: Returns `true` if the file stream refers to an interactive terminal.
- `fn (f: File) poll(timeout_ms: i64 = 0) -> bool`: Polls the file stream for readability up to `timeout_ms` milliseconds (`EINTR`-safe).
- `fn (mut f: File) read_into(mut buf: []byte) -> usize!`: Reads up to `buf.len()` bytes from the file stream into `buf`.
- `fn (mut f: File) read_exact(exact_bytes: usize) -> []byte!`: Reads exactly `exact_bytes` from the file stream or returns an error on premature EOF.
- `fn (mut f: File) read_bytes(max_bytes: usize = 67108864) -> []byte!`: Reads up to `max_bytes` from the file stream into a new byte slice.
- `fn (mut f: File) read_text(max_bytes: usize = 67108864) -> str!`: Reads up to `max_bytes` from the file stream as a UTF-8 string.
- `fn (mut f: File) read_bytes_until(delim: byte, max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> []byte!`: Reads bytes from the file stream up to and including `delim` (or `max_bytes`).
- `fn (mut f: File) read_text_until(delim: str, max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> str!`: Reads text from the file stream up to and including the first byte of `delim` (or `max_bytes`).
- `fn (mut f: File) read_line(max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> str?`: Reads the next line from the file stream (stripping `\r\n` / `\n`), or `none` on EOF.
- `fn (mut f: File) read_lines() -> []str!`: Reads all remaining lines from the file stream into a string slice.
- `fn (mut f: File) write_bytes(data: []byte) -> usize!`: Writes all bytes in `data` to the file stream, looping across partial writes and `EINTR`.
- `fn (mut f: File) write_text(text: str) -> usize!`: Writes a UTF-8 string to the file stream, looping across partial writes and `EINTR`.
- `fn (mut f: File) seek(offset: i64, whence: SeekWhence = SeekWhence::Start) -> i64!`: Seeks within file to offset from Start, Current, or End.
- `fn (mut f: File) tell() -> i64!`: Returns current byte offset within file stream.
- `fn (mut f: File) flush() -> void!`: Flushes C stdio buffers (`stdout`/`stderr`) when wrapping standard descriptors (`fs.File` is otherwise an unbuffered OS descriptor; use `sync()` to flush OS buffers to storage).
- `fn (mut f: File) sync() -> void!`: Flushes OS buffers for this file to durable storage (`F_FULLFSYNC`/`fsync`/`FlushFileBuffers`).
- `fn (mut f: File) close() -> void`: Closes open file handle.
- `fn dirname(path: str) -> str` (call: `fs.dirname`): Returns directory portion of a filesystem path.
- `fn basename(path: str) -> str` (call: `fs.basename`): Returns file name portion of a filesystem path.
- `fn extension(path: str) -> str` (call: `fs.extension`): Returns file extension including leading dot.
- `fn exists(path: str) -> bool` (call: `fs.exists`): Returns `true` if the path exists on disk.
- `fn is_dir(path: str) -> bool` (call: `fs.is_dir`): Returns `true` if `path` exists and is a directory.
- `fn is_file(path: str) -> bool` (call: `fs.is_file`): Returns `true` if `path` exists and is a regular file.
- `fn mkdir_all(path: str) -> void!` (call: `fs.mkdir_all`): Recursively creates a directory and all parent directories.
- `fn remove(path: str) -> void!` (call: `fs.remove`): Removes a file or directory tree recursively.
- `fn list_dir(path: str) -> []str!` (call: `fs.list_dir`): Lists sorted filenames inside a directory.

### `import "core:json"` (alias: `json`)
Uses `json:"..."` struct tags (with automatic field-name fallback and `T?` optional field support) to emit specialized `simdjson::ondemand` parsers and fast `std::format` serializers with zero runtime reflection overhead, along with a zero-dependency dynamic DOM `json.Value`.
Types:
- `Value`: A parsed JSON value of any shape, from `json.parse_dynamic`; inspect it with its methods.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn parse[T](payload: []byte | str) -> T!` (call: `json.parse`): Parses UTF-8 JSON into a struct `T` using `simdjson::ondemand`.
- `fn stringify[T](val: T) -> str` (call: `json.stringify`): Serializes a struct `T` (`str`, `u64`, `i64`, `i32`, `f64`, `bool`, `T?`, slices, nested structs) into a JSON string.
- `fn schema[T]() -> str` (call: `json.schema`): Generates a Draft 2020-12 / OpenAI Strict Mode / MCP JSON Schema string for struct `T` using `json:"..."` and `desc:"..."` tags.
- `fn escape_string(s: str) -> str` (call: `json.escape_string`): Escapes quotes, backslashes, and control characters for JSON strings.
- `fn parse_dynamic(payload: str) -> Value!` (call: `json.parse_dynamic`): Parses arbitrary JSON into a recursive dynamic DOM `Value`.
- `fn stringify_dynamic(val: Value, indent: i32 = 0) -> str` (call: `json.stringify_dynamic`): Serializes a dynamic DOM `Value` into compact or indented JSON.

### `import "core:keychain"` (alias: `keychain`)
Cross-platform OS credential storage backed by `Security.framework` (`SecItemAdd` / `SecItemCopyMatching` / `SecItemDelete`) on macOS & iOS, `libsecret` (`secret-tool`) on Linux, and Windows Credential Manager (`CredWriteW` / `CredReadW`) on Windows, plus Face ID / Touch ID and device passcode user-presence verification via Apple `LocalAuthentication`.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn set(service: str, account: str, secret: str) -> void!` (call: `keychain.set`): Stores or updates a generic password for `(service, account)` in the OS keychain.
- `fn get(service: str, account: str) -> str!` (call: `keychain.get`): Retrieves the secret stored for `(service, account)` from the OS keychain.
- `fn delete_password(service: str, account: str) -> void!` (call: `keychain.delete_password`): Removes the credential entry for `(service, account)` from the OS keychain.
- `fn authenticate_biometric(reason: str, allow_passcode: bool = true) -> bool!` (call: `keychain.authenticate_biometric`): Prompts for Face ID / Touch ID (with optional device passcode fallback when `allow_passcode` is `true`) via Apple `LocalAuthentication`; returns `Err` on unsupported platforms or when invoked on a GUI main thread.

### `import "core:log"` (alias: `log`)
Leveled logging (`debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`) with `Level` (`Debug`, `Info`, `Warn`, `Error`), `Format` (`Text`, `Json`), and structured key-value attributes.
Types:
- `Level`: Minimum severity for `log.set_level`.
- `Format`: Output format for `log.set_format`.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn set_level(l: Level)` (call: `log.set_level`): Sets the minimum logging severity threshold (`log.Level::Debug`, `Info`, `Warn`, `Error`).
- `fn get_level() -> Level` (call: `log.get_level`): Returns the current minimum logging severity threshold.
- `fn set_format(f: Format)` (call: `log.set_format`): Sets the log output format (`log.Format::Text` or `log.Format::Json`).
- `fn get_format() -> Format` (call: `log.get_format`): Returns the current log output format.
- `fn debug(msg: str, ...attrs: any)` (call: `log.debug`): Logs a debug message with optional key-value attribute pairs.
- `fn info(msg: str, ...attrs: any)` (call: `log.info`): Logs an informational message with optional key-value attribute pairs.
- `fn warn(msg: str, ...attrs: any)` (call: `log.warn`): Logs a warning message with optional key-value attribute pairs.
- `fn error(msg: str, ...attrs: any)` (call: `log.error`): Logs an error message with optional key-value attribute pairs.

### `import "core:math"` (alias: `math`)
Mathematical constants (`math.PI`, `math.E`, `math.TAU`, `math.SQRT_2`, `math.LN_2`, `math.LN_10`) and functions with no natural receiver (`atan2`, `hypot`, `gcd`, `lcm`). Single-value operations are methods on the number itself (`x.abs()`, `f.sqrt()`, `x.clamp(lo, hi)`, `a.checked_add(b)`); type limits and parsing are associated with the type (`i32.MAX`, `f64.NAN`, `i32.parse(s)`). See the builtin method reference.
Functions & Methods:
- `const PI: f64` (call: `math.PI`): Ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter (π).
- `const E: f64` (call: `math.E`): Euler's number (e).
- `const TAU: f64` (call: `math.TAU`): Full turn in radians (2π).
- `const SQRT_2: f64` (call: `math.SQRT_2`): Square root of 2.
- `const LN_2: f64` (call: `math.LN_2`): Natural logarithm of 2.
- `const LN_10: f64` (call: `math.LN_10`): Natural logarithm of 10.
- `fn atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64` (call: `math.atan2`): Angle of the point `(x, y)` from the positive x-axis, in radians (`-π..=π`).
- `fn hypot(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64` (call: `math.hypot`): `sqrt(x*x + y*y)` without intermediate overflow or underflow.
- `fn gcd(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` (call: `math.gcd`): Greatest common divisor (non-negative); `gcd(0, 0) == 0`. Panics for the minimum `i64`.
- `fn lcm(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64` (call: `math.lcm`): Least common multiple (non-negative); panics on overflow.

### `import "core:net"` (alias: `net`)
RAII TCP client, listener, and connected socketpair handles backed by BSD `AF_INET` / `AF_UNIX` sockets with non-blocking `poll` timeouts and strict `_bytes` / `_text` I/O symmetry.
Types:
- `TcpListener`: A listening TCP socket; `accept()` returns a `TcpConn` per client.
- `TcpConn`: A connected TCP stream, closed when it goes out of scope.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn listen(port: u16 = 0, host: str = "0.0.0.0") -> TcpListener!` (call: `net.listen`): Binds a TCP listener on `host:port` (`0` picks an ephemeral port; the default host is every interface).
- `fn (ln: TcpListener) port() -> u16`: Returns the bound TCP port.
- `fn (mut ln: TcpListener) accept() -> TcpConn!`: Accepts an incoming TCP connection with a safe poll timeout.
- `fn connect(host: str, port: u16) -> TcpConn!` (call: `net.connect`): Connects a `TcpConn` to `host:port`.
- `fn socketpair() -> (TcpConn, TcpConn)!` (call: `net.socketpair`): Creates a connected pair of full-duplex `TcpConn` stream sockets.
- `fn (c: TcpConn) remote_addr() -> str`: The peer address of an accepted connection (`203.0.113.7`, `2001:db8::1`; IPv4-mapped IPv6 peers are reported as IPv4), or the host a client connection dialed.
- `fn (c: TcpConn) fd() -> i32`: Returns the underlying socket file descriptor (`-1` if closed).
- `fn (c: TcpConn) is_open() -> bool`: Returns `true` if the socket connection is open.
- `fn (c: TcpConn) poll(timeout_ms: i64 = 0) -> bool`: Polls the socket for readability up to `timeout_ms` milliseconds (`EINTR`-safe).
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) write_bytes(payload: []byte) -> usize!`: Writes all bytes in `payload` to the TCP/TLS connection, looping across partial sends and `EINTR`.
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) write_text(text: str) -> usize!`: Writes a UTF-8 string to the TCP/TLS connection, looping across partial sends and `EINTR`.
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) read_into(mut buf: []byte) -> usize!`: Reads up to `buf.len()` bytes from the socket into `buf` (`EINTR`-safe).
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) read_bytes(max_bytes: usize = 4096) -> []byte!`: Reads up to `max_bytes` from the socket into a new byte slice.
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) read_exact(exact_bytes: usize) -> []byte!`: Reads exactly `exact_bytes` from the socket or returns an error on premature EOF.
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) read_text(max_bytes: usize = 4096) -> str!`: Reads up to `max_bytes` from the socket as a UTF-8 string.
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) read_bytes_until(delim: byte, max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> []byte!`: Reads bytes from the socket up to and including `delim` (or `max_bytes`).
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) read_text_until(delim: str, max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> str!`: Reads text from the socket up to and including the first byte of `delim` (or `max_bytes`).
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) read_line(max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> str?`: Reads a newline-delimited line up to `max_bytes` from the socket, or `none` on EOF.
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) set_timeout_ms(ms: i32) -> void`: Sets socket read/write timeout in milliseconds (`0` for blocking).
- `fn (mut c: TcpConn) close() -> void`: Closes the TCP socket connection.

### `import "core:net/http"` (alias: `http`)
RFC 9112 HTTP/1.1 & HTTPS client (`get`, `post`, `request`), wire parser (`parse_request`), response serializer (`Response`), HTTP/HTTPS server (`make(http.Server, port)`, `make(http.Server, port, tls: http.TlsConfig{...})`, per-connection `http.ServerLimits`), and request router (`make_router`) with integrated WebSocket route upgrade (`Router.ws`).
Types:
- `Request`: An HTTP request, as a handler receives it or as you build one to send.
- `Response`: An HTTP response; build one with `http.Response.text`, `.json`, `.html` or `.redirect`.
- `Router`: Maps method and path patterns to handlers; registering a route returns the router, so calls chain.
- `HttpServer`: An HTTP server bound to a port (`make(http.Server, port)`); `serve_in_background` runs it and `stop` ends it.
- `Server`: The name `make(http.Server, port)` constructs; the same type as `http.HttpServer`.
- `SseEvent`: One server-sent event.
- `ServerLimits`: Per-connection limits for `http.Server` (with keep-alive and event-loop limits); pass to `server.set_limits(...)`. The server waits on idle and slow connections in an event loop, so `workers` is only how many handlers run at once; `workers = 0` keeps the default (twice the core count, at least 4). An idle keep-alive connection closes after `keepalive_timeout_ms` (0 turns keep-alive off) or after `max_requests_per_conn` requests. Each WebSocket session runs on its own thread, up to `max_websockets`. Over `max_connections` open connections or `max_pending` requests waiting for a worker, a client gets 503.
- `TlsConfig`: Server certificate for `make(http.Server, port, tls: ...)`: set `cert_file`/`key_file`, or `cert_pem`/`key_pem` for in-memory PEM.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn get(url: str, headers: map[str]str = {}, verify_peer: bool = true, timeout_ms: i64 = 30000) -> Response!` (call: `http.get`): Executes an HTTP or HTTPS GET request against a target URL within the end-to-end `timeout_ms` deadline (`0` disables).
- `fn post(url: str, body: str, content_type: str = "application/json", headers: map[str]str = {}, verify_peer: bool = true, timeout_ms: i64 = 30000) -> Response!` (call: `http.post`): Executes an HTTP or HTTPS POST request with payload body within `timeout_ms` (`0` disables).
- `fn request(method: str, url: str, body: str = "", content_type: str = "", headers: map[str]str = {}, verify_peer: bool = true, ca_file: str = "", timeout_ms: i64 = 30000) -> Response!` (call: `http.request`): Executes an arbitrary HTTP or HTTPS request (PUT, DELETE, PATCH, etc.) within `timeout_ms` (`0` disables).
- `fn post_sse(url: str, body: str, headers: map[str]str = {}, on_event: fn(SseEvent) -> bool, verify_peer: bool = true, ca_file: str = "", timeout_ms: i64 = 30000) -> Response!` (call: `http.post_sse`): Streams an HTTP/HTTPS POST response using Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`) and chunked transfer encoding, invoking `on_event` for each event.
- `fn serve_in_background(port: u16, handler: fn(Request) -> Response | Router, tls: TlsConfig = {}, host: str = "0.0.0.0") -> HttpServer!` (call: `http.serve_in_background`): Binds a server on `host:port`, starts its background event loop, and returns the live `HttpServer` handle.
- `fn make(port: u16 = 0, tls: TlsConfig = {}, host: str = "0.0.0.0") -> HttpServer!`: `make(http.Server, port)` creates an HTTP server listening on `host:port` (`0` picks an ephemeral port); `make(http.Server, port, tls: http.TlsConfig{cert_file: c, key_file: k})` serves HTTPS, and `host: "127.0.0.1"` restricts binding to loopback.
- `fn make() -> Router`: `make(http.Router)` creates an independent HTTP & WebSocket request router supporting path parameters (`:id`) and wildcards (`*path`).
- `fn parse_request(raw: str) -> Request!` (call: `http.parse_request`): Parses raw HTTP/1.1 wire text into a structured Request model.
- `fn Response.text(code: i32, payload: str) -> Response`: Creates an HTTP Response with text/plain content-type and standard status reason.
- `fn Response.json(code: i32, json_str: str) -> Response`: Creates an HTTP Response with application/json content-type.
- `fn Response.html(code: i32, html: str) -> Response`: Creates an HTTP Response with text/html content-type.
- `fn Response.redirect(location: str, code: i32 = 302) -> Response`: Creates an HTTP redirect Response setting Location header.
- `fn (mut r: Router) get(pattern: str, handler: fn(Request) -> Response) -> Router`: Registers an HTTP GET route with optional path parameters (`:id`) or wildcards (`*path`).
- `fn (mut r: Router) post(pattern: str, handler: fn(Request) -> Response) -> Router`: Registers an HTTP POST route handler.
- `fn (mut r: Router) put(pattern: str, handler: fn(Request) -> Response) -> Router`: Registers an HTTP PUT route handler.
- `fn (mut r: Router) delete_(pattern: str, handler: fn(Request) -> Response) -> Router`: Registers an HTTP DELETE route handler.
- `fn (mut r: Router) ws(pattern: str, handler: fn(Request, mut websocket.Conn) -> void) -> Router`: Registers a WebSocket route that automatically upgrades matching HTTP requests and invokes `handler(req, mut ws)`.
- `fn (r: Router) dispatch(req: Request) -> Response`: Dispatches an HTTP request through the router in-memory without open network sockets.
- `fn (mut r: Router) use(mw: fn(mut Request) -> Response?) -> Router`: Registers pre-routing middleware that can short-circuit or validate HTTP and WebSocket upgrade requests.
- `type ServerLimits struct { header_timeout_ms: i32 = 10000, body_timeout_ms: i32 = 30000, max_body_bytes: usize = 10485760, workers: usize = 0, max_pending: usize = 128, keepalive_timeout_ms: i32 = 5000, max_requests_per_conn: usize = 1000, max_websockets: usize = 1024, max_connections: usize = 10000 }` (call: `http.ServerLimits`): Per-connection server limits. Idle and slow connections wait in the server's event loop, so `workers` is how many handlers run at once. Omitted fields keep their defaults; `workers = 0` keeps the default (twice the core count, at least 4). `keepalive_timeout_ms = 0` turns keep-alive off.
- `type TlsConfig struct { cert_file: str, key_file: str, cert_pem: str, key_pem: str }` (call: `http.TlsConfig`): Server certificate for `make(http.Server, port, tls: ...)`: set `cert_file` / `key_file`, or `cert_pem` / `key_pem` for in-memory PEM.
- `fn (mut s: HttpServer) set_limits(limits: ServerLimits)`: Replaces the per-connection limits: `http.ServerLimits{header_timeout_ms, body_timeout_ms, max_body_bytes, workers, max_pending, keepalive_timeout_ms, max_requests_per_conn, max_websockets, max_connections}`; omitted fields keep their defaults.
- `fn (mut s: HttpServer) enable_tls_files(cert_file: str, key_file: str) -> void!`: Enables TLS on the server using certificate and private key PEM files.
- `fn (mut s: HttpServer) enable_tls_pem(cert_pem: str, key_pem: str) -> void!`: Enables TLS on the server using in-memory certificate and private key PEM strings.
- `fn (mut s: HttpServer) serve_in_background(handler: fn(Request) -> Response | Router) -> void`: Starts a non-blocking background accept loop serving HTTP and WebSocket upgrade requests.
- `fn (s: HttpServer) port() -> u16`: Returns the port the server is listening on (useful after binding port 0).
- `fn (mut s: HttpServer) stop() -> void`: Gracefully closes the listening socket and stops worker threads.
- `fn (req: Request) param(key: str, fallback: str = "") -> str`: Retrieves a named route path parameter extracted by the router.
- `fn (req: Request) query(key: str, fallback: str = "") -> str`: Retrieves a decoded URL query parameter.
- `fn (req: Request) header(key: str, fallback: str = "") -> str`: Performs a case-insensitive header lookup.

### `import "core:net/ipc"` (alias: `ipc`)
Same-machine local IPC backed by `0600` Unix domain sockets (`AF_UNIX`) on macOS & Linux and owner-restricted Named Pipes (`PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS`) on Windows, with OS-verified peer process and user credentials (`peer_credentials`) and full `_bytes`/`_text` streaming.
Types:
- `Listener`: A local IPC server bound to a Unix domain socket (`0600`) or Windows named pipe (same-user ACL); `accept()` returns a `Conn` per client.
- `Conn`: A connected full-duplex local IPC stream, closed automatically when it goes out of scope.
- `PeerCred`: Verified OS credentials of a local IPC peer from `conn.peer_credentials()`.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn endpoint(name: str) -> str` (call: `ipc.endpoint`): Resolves a logical service name into a private per-user OS IPC endpoint (`AF_UNIX` path on POSIX, owner-scoped Named Pipe on Windows).
- `fn listen(endpoint: str) -> Listener!` (call: `ipc.listen`): Creates a private local IPC server (`0600` socket on POSIX after stale-socket check; owner-only Named Pipe on Windows).
- `fn connect(endpoint: str, timeout_ms: i32 = 5000) -> Conn!` (call: `ipc.connect`): Connects to a local IPC listener endpoint within `timeout_ms`.
- `fn (mut l: Listener) accept() -> Conn!`: Waits for and accepts an incoming local IPC client connection.
- `fn (l: Listener) endpoint() -> str`: Returns the bound endpoint path or pipe name.
- `fn (l: Listener) is_open() -> bool`: Returns `true` if the IPC listener is still open.
- `fn (mut l: Listener) close() -> void`: Closes the listener and removes its POSIX socket path (existing accepted `Conn` handles remain usable).
- `fn (c: Conn) is_open() -> bool`: Returns `true` if the IPC connection handle is open.
- `fn (c: Conn) poll(timeout_ms: i64 = 0) -> bool`: Polls the IPC stream for readability up to `timeout_ms` milliseconds.
- `fn (mut c: Conn) set_timeout_ms(ms: i32) -> void`: Sets read/write I/O timeout in milliseconds (`0` for blocking).
- `fn (mut c: Conn) write_bytes(payload: []byte) -> usize!`: Writes all bytes in `payload` to the IPC stream.
- `fn (mut c: Conn) write_text(text: str) -> usize!`: Writes a UTF-8 string to the IPC stream.
- `fn (mut c: Conn) read_into(mut buf: []byte) -> usize!`: Reads up to `buf.len()` bytes from the IPC stream into `buf`.
- `fn (mut c: Conn) read_bytes(max_bytes: usize = 4096) -> []byte!`: Reads up to `max_bytes` bytes from the IPC stream.
- `fn (mut c: Conn) read_exact(exact_bytes: usize) -> []byte!`: Reads exactly `exact_bytes` from the IPC stream or fails on premature EOF.
- `fn (mut c: Conn) read_text(max_bytes: usize = 4096) -> str!`: Reads up to `max_bytes` from the IPC stream as a UTF-8 string.
- `fn (mut c: Conn) read_bytes_until(delim: byte, max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> []byte!`: Reads bytes up to and including `delim` (or `max_bytes`).
- `fn (mut c: Conn) read_text_until(delim: str, max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> str!`: Reads text up to and including `delim` (or `max_bytes`).
- `fn (mut c: Conn) read_line(max_bytes: usize = 65536) -> str?`: Reads the next line from the IPC stream (stripping `\r\n` / `\n`), or `none` on EOF.
- `fn (c: Conn) peer_credentials() -> PeerCred!`: Queries OS-authenticated peer credentials (`pid`, `same_user`, `uid`).
- `fn (mut c: Conn) close() -> void`: Closes the IPC stream connection.

### `import "core:net/tls"` (alias: `tls`)
Zero-build-flag TLS 1.2/1.3 client/server encryption, SNI hostname negotiation, X.509 peer certificate verification, PEM certificate loading, and in-memory self-signed certificate generation.
Types:
- `ServerContext`: A TLS server configuration (certificate and key) that wraps accepted connections.
- `CertKeyPair`: A certificate and its private key, in PEM form.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn available() -> bool` (call: `tls.available`): Returns `true` if the OpenSSL (`libssl` / `libcrypto`) runtime bridge is available.
- `fn generate_self_signed_pem(common_name: str = "localhost", days: i32 = 365) -> CertKeyPair!` (call: `tls.generate_self_signed_pem`): Generates an in-memory RSA-2048 X.509v3 self-signed certificate and private key in PEM format.
- `fn wrap_client(mut conn: TcpConn, server_name: str = "", verify_peer: bool = true, ca_file: str = "") -> void!` (call: `tls.wrap_client`): Upgrades an open `TcpConn` to a client TLS session with SNI and optional X.509 certificate verification.
- `fn connect(host: str, port: u16 = 443, verify_peer: bool = true, ca_file: str = "") -> TcpConn!` (call: `tls.connect`): Connects a TCP socket to `host:port` and completes a TLS client handshake.
- `fn ServerContext.from_files(cert_file: str, key_file: str) -> ServerContext!`: Creates a TLS server context from X.509 certificate chain and private key PEM files on disk.
- `fn ServerContext.from_pem(cert_pem: str, key_pem: str) -> ServerContext!`: Creates a TLS server context directly from in-memory certificate and private key PEM strings.
- `fn (ctx: ServerContext) wrap_server(mut conn: TcpConn) -> void!`: Performs a server-side TLS handshake (`SSL_accept`) on an accepted `TcpConn`.

### `import "core:net/url"` (alias: `url`)
RFC 3986 URL parsing with component extraction (scheme, host, port, path, query, fragment), form-urlencoded query parameter maps, and percent encoding/decoding.
Types:
- `Url`: A parsed URL, from `url.parse`.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn parse(raw: str) -> Url!` (call: `url.parse`): Parses an RFC 3986 URL string into component fields and query parameters (`https` and `wss` default to port 443).
- `fn encode(s: str) -> str` (call: `url.encode`): Percent-encodes a string for safe use in URL path or query strings.
- `fn decode(s: str) -> str` (call: `url.decode`): Decodes a percent-encoded URL string.

### `import "core:net/websocket"` (alias: `websocket`)
RFC 6455 full-duplex `ws://` and `wss://` WebSocket client (`connect`, with `verify_peer: false` for self-signed certificates), standalone server (`make(websocket.Server, port)`, `tls: websocket.TlsConfig{...}` for `wss://`), and connection upgrade handler (`upgrade`) with automated framing, client masking, and Ping/Pong management.
Types:
- `Conn`: An open WebSocket connection; messages are `str` (`recv_text`) or `[]byte` (`recv_binary`).
- `Server`: A WebSocket server bound to a port (`make(websocket.Server, port)`); each connection runs on its own session thread, so handlers run concurrently.
- `ServerLimits`: Limits for `websocket.Server`; pass to `server.set_limits(...)`. Each connection runs on its own session thread, up to `max_websockets` (over it a client gets 503); `header_timeout_ms` bounds the TLS handshake and the upgrade request; `max_frame_size` is each session's largest accepted frame. A field set to 0 keeps its default.
- `TlsConfig`: Server certificate for `make(websocket.Server, port, tls: ...)`; the same type as `http.TlsConfig`.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn connect(url: str, verify_peer: bool = true) -> Conn!` (call: `websocket.connect`): Establishes a `ws://` or `wss://` WebSocket connection and completes the RFC 6455 handshake.
- `type TlsConfig struct { cert_file: str, key_file: str, cert_pem: str, key_pem: str }` (call: `websocket.TlsConfig`): Server certificate for `make(websocket.Server, port, tls: ...)`; the same type as `http.TlsConfig`.
- `fn make(port: u16 = 0, tls: TlsConfig = {}, host: str = "0.0.0.0") -> Server!`: `make(websocket.Server, port)` creates a standalone WebSocket server listening on `host:port` (`0` picks an ephemeral port); add `tls: websocket.TlsConfig{...}` for `wss://`, and `host: "127.0.0.1"` for loopback-only.
- `fn upgrade(req: Request, mut conn: TcpConn) -> Conn!` (call: `websocket.upgrade`): Upgrades an incoming HTTP or HTTPS connection to a WebSocket connection.
- `fn pair() -> (Conn, Conn)!` (call: `websocket.pair`): Creates an in-process full-duplex WebSocket client/server loopback pair.
- `fn (mut ws: Conn) send_text(msg: str) -> void!`: Sends a UTF-8 text frame to the peer (masked if client).
- `fn (mut ws: Conn) send_binary(data: []byte) -> void!`: Sends a binary data frame to the peer (masked if client).
- `fn (mut ws: Conn) recv_text() -> str!`: Receives the next text frame from the peer, automatically responding to Ping frames with Pong.
- `fn (mut ws: Conn) recv_binary() -> []byte!`: Receives the next binary frame from the peer.
- `fn (mut ws: Conn) ping(payload: str = "") -> void!`: Sends a Ping control frame to check peer liveness.
- `fn (mut ws: Conn) set_timeout_ms(ms: i32) -> void`: Sets read/write socket timeout in milliseconds (`0` for blocking).
- `fn (mut ws: Conn) close(code: u16 = 1000, reason: str = "")`: Initiates a clean RFC 6455 closure handshake and closes the socket.
- `fn (ws: Conn) is_open() -> bool`: Returns true if the WebSocket connection is open.
- `fn (mut s: Server) accept() -> Conn!`: Accepts one incoming connection, completes the TLS and RFC 6455 upgrade handshake, and returns a `Conn`.
- `type ServerLimits struct { max_websockets: usize = 1024, header_timeout_ms: i32 = 10000, max_frame_size: usize = 16777216 }` (call: `websocket.ServerLimits`): Limits for `websocket.Server`: open sessions (over `max_websockets` a client gets 503), the deadline for the TLS handshake and upgrade request, and the largest accepted frame. Omitted or 0 fields keep their defaults.
- `fn (mut s: Server) set_limits(limits: ServerLimits)`: Replaces the server's limits: `websocket.ServerLimits{max_websockets, header_timeout_ms, max_frame_size}`; call it before serving.
- `fn (mut s: Server) serve_once(handler: fn(mut Conn) -> void) -> void`: Accepts and serves a single WebSocket connection with `handler`, on the calling thread.
- `fn (mut s: Server) listen_and_serve(handler: fn(mut Conn) -> void) -> void`: Runs a blocking accept loop; each connection is upgraded and served on its own session thread, so `handler` runs concurrently for several clients and state it shares must be synchronized. Over `max_websockets` open sessions a client gets 503.
- `fn (mut s: Server) serve_in_background(handler: fn(mut Conn) -> void) -> void`: Starts the accept loop on a background thread; like `listen_and_serve`, each connection gets its own session thread and `handler` runs concurrently.
- `fn (mut s: Server) stop() -> void`: Stops the accept loop, shuts the open sessions down and waits for their handlers to return.

### `import "core:os"` (alias: `os`)
Process environment inspection, working directory and persistent OS app directory queries (`data_dir`, `cache_dir`, `documents_dir`), safe external URL launching (`open_url`), standard stream handles (`os.stdin()`, `os.stdout()`, `os.stderr()`), RAII pipes (`os.pipe()`), raw terminal control (`is_tty`, `term_size`, `make(os.RawTerminal)`, `on_signal`), and subprocess execution (`command`, `exec_output`).
Types:
- `ExecResult`: The outcome of a finished subprocess (`os.command`).
- `TermSize`: A terminal's size in character cells.
- `RawTerminal`: The terminal in raw mode (no echo, no line buffering); restored when it goes out of scope.
Functions & Methods:
- `fn args() -> []str` (call: `os.args`): Returns the command-line arguments passed to the current process.
- `fn exit(code: i32)` (call: `os.exit`): Terminates the current process immediately with status `code`.
- `fn getenv(key: str) -> str?` (call: `os.getenv`): Reads environment variable `key`, returning `none` if unset.
- `fn setenv(key: str, value: str)` (call: `os.setenv`): Sets environment variable `key` to `value` in the current process.
- `fn cwd() -> str` (call: `os.cwd`): Returns the current working directory path.
- `fn data_dir(app: str = "") -> str!` (call: `os.data_dir`): Returns (and creates with `0700` permissions if missing) the OS-standard persistent application data directory (`Application Support` on Apple, `XDG_DATA_HOME` on Linux, `FOLDERID_RoamingAppData` on Windows).
- `fn cache_dir(app: str = "") -> str!` (call: `os.cache_dir`): Returns (and creates with `0700` permissions if missing) the OS-standard cache directory (`Library/Caches` on Apple, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` on Linux, `FOLDERID_LocalAppData\\Cache` on Windows).
- `fn documents_dir() -> str!` (call: `os.documents_dir`): Returns (and creates with `0700` permissions if missing) the user's OS-standard Documents directory (`~/Documents` on Apple, `XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR` on Linux, `FOLDERID_Documents` on Windows).
- `fn open_url(url: str) -> void!` (call: `os.open_url`): Opens a validated external URL (`http://`, `https://`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, or custom schemes; rejects `file:` / `javascript:` schemes and control characters) via the OS handler without shell interpretation.
- `fn getpid() -> i64` (call: `os.getpid`): Returns the process ID (PID) of the current process.
- `fn stdin() -> File` (call: `os.stdin`): Returns a non-owning `fs.File` stream handle wrapping standard input (FD 0).
- `fn stdout() -> File` (call: `os.stdout`): Returns a non-owning `fs.File` stream handle wrapping standard output (FD 1).
- `fn stderr() -> File` (call: `os.stderr`): Returns a non-owning `fs.File` stream handle wrapping standard error (FD 2).
- `fn pipe() -> (File, File)!` (call: `os.pipe`): Creates an OS pipe returning an owning `(reader, writer)` tuple of `fs.File` handles with `FD_CLOEXEC` enabled.
- `fn is_tty() -> bool` (call: `os.is_tty`): Returns `true` if standard input refers to an interactive terminal (or call `.is_tty()` on any `fs.File`).
- `fn term_size() -> TermSize` (call: `os.term_size`): Queries terminal dimensions (`cols`, `rows`) via `TIOCGWINSZ`, defaulting to 80x24 if not a TTY.
